sort() with a comparator returning true/false gives a wrong order
content:
I am sorting users by score and the result is only partly ordered.

```javascript
const users = [
  { name: 'a', score: 10 },
  { name: 'b', score: 3 },
  { name: 'c', score: 42 },
  { name: 'd', score: 7 },
];

users.sort((x, y) => x.score > y.score);
console.log(users.map(u => u.score)); // [10, 3, 42, 7] in Chrome
```

I expected `[3, 7, 10, 42]`. With four items nothing moves at all; with twenty items I get something that is almost sorted but not quite, which is what made me look. The same code seemed fine in an older project, so I assumed the comparator was valid. What exactly does `sort` do with a boolean, and why does the result depend on the array length?

Bootstrap 5.3 data-bs-theme=dark does not affect my custom card styles
content: I switched the app to Bootstrap 5.3's colour modes by putting `data-bs-theme="dark"` on `<html>`. Every built-in component flips correctly: navbar, buttons, form controls, the table. My own `.stat-card` class stays white with dark text, so half the dashboard is unreadable. The card styles are in my own stylesheet, loaded after Bootstrap, and they set `background: #fff` and `color: #212529` because that is what I copied from the design. I tried adding a `[data-bs-theme="dark"] .stat-card` override, which works, but I now have to duplicate every custom rule and the two themes drift apart every time the design changes. Bootstrap 5.3.3, no Sass build, just the CDN CSS. Is there a supported way to make my own components follow the theme the way the built-in ones do?

title: jQuery click handler does not fire on rows added after page load
jQuery 3.7: .success is not a function on my $.ajax call
content: An old admin page throws `TypeError: $.ajax(...).success is not a function` on every save since we bumped jQuery from 1.12 to 3.7.1. The call is the classic chained form: `$.ajax({...}).success(fn).error(fn)`. Nothing else about the request changed, and the network tab shows the POST going out and coming back 200, so it is only the callback wiring that broke. I searched our bundle and there are about forty of these across the codebase, plus a couple of `.complete()`. I know these were deprecated at some point, but I want to be sure I replace them with the right names rather than guessing, and I would like to know whether the replacement callbacks receive the same argument order, because some of our handlers read the third argument. What is the current equivalent for each of the three?

NG0100 ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError from a template getter
content: My form component throws NG0100 in dev mode: Expression has changed after it was checked. Previous value for 'disabled': 'false'. Current value: 'true'. The binding is `[disabled]="isBusy"` on the submit button, and `isBusy` is a getter that returns `this.form.pending || this.saving`. It only happens when the async validator on the email field is still running at the moment the view is first checked, so it is not reproducible on every load, and production builds do not throw because the second check is skipped. Angular 19, default change detection, no OnPush anywhere in this component tree. Wrapping the state update in `setTimeout` makes the error go away, which I understand pushes it to the next tick, but I would like to know why the getter produces a different value inside the same cycle and what the recommended fix is when the value genuinely depends on form status.

title: Destructuring a $state object in Svelte 5 breaks reactivity
Svelte 5 build fails on on:click and the |preventDefault modifier
content: After running the Svelte 5 migration on a mid-size app most components compile, but a handful of forms fail the build with: `Event modifiers are not supported in runes mode` and, on other lines, a deprecation error about `on:click` no longer being valid element event syntax. The offending markup is the usual `<form on:submit|preventDefault={save}>` and `<button on:click|once={openOnce}>`. I know the plain `on:click` to `onclick` rename, and the codemod did most of those, but it left every line that carries a modifier untouched, which suggests there is no mechanical equivalent. Svelte 5.20, SvelteKit 2. What is the intended replacement for `preventDefault`, `stopPropagation` and `once` now, and is there still a way to get the `once` behaviour without tracking a boolean by hand?

title: dialog closes on submit but returnValue is always an empty string
content:
I need to know which button closed the dialog and `returnValue` never carries it.

```xml
<dialog id="confirm">
  <form method="dialog">
    <button value="cancel">Cancel</button>
    <button value="delete">Delete</button>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

```javascript
confirmEl.addEventListener('close', () => {
  console.log(confirmEl.returnValue); // '' every time
});
```

The dialog does close on either button, so the `method="dialog"` part is working. Chrome 133 and Firefox 135 behave the same. The buttons are inside the form and both have a `value`. What I eventually noticed is that our design system component renders them with `type="button"`. Is that the reason the submitter is never recorded, and is `returnValue` the right thing to read at all, or should I be listening for something else?

content:
I render editable rows and remove the middle one; the inputs below shift their text up by one. ```javascript {rows.map((row, i) => (
    • ))} ``` With rows A, B, C, deleting B leaves two rows whose inputs read A and B, while the state array is correctly [A, C]. React 19.2. Switching `defaultValue` to `value` plus an onChange handler fixes the display, but I would rather understand the cause than change the control mode, because the same list also has an uncontrolled file input that has the same issue. Build fails: useSearchParams() should be wrapped in a suspense boundary
content: `next dev` is perfectly happy and `next build` refuses to finish. The error is: useSearchParams() should be wrapped in a suspense boundary at page "/search". The component reading the params is a small client component that renders the active filter chips, and it is imported into the page like any other component. I tried marking the page itself with `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, which does make the build pass, but that opts the entire route out of static rendering, and the rest of the page is static content I would like prerendered. Next.js 16, App Router. I do not fully understand what the boundary is protecting against during prerender, or how big it should be — does it go around just the chips component, or around everything that could read from the URL?

title: ERR_REQUIRE_ESM after updating a dependency in my CommonJS build script
content: One of our build scripts started failing after a routine dependency bump. The error is: Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module /app/node_modules/chalk/source/index.js from /app/scripts/report.js not supported. Instead change the require of index.js to a dynamic import() which is available in all CommonJS modules. The script is a plain `.js` file using `require`, the package has no `"type"` field, and the dependency's changelog says it is now ESM-only. Node 22. I tried adding `"type": "module"` to package.json, which fixed this script and broke four others that use `__dirname` and `module.exports`. Pinning the old version works for now but is obviously temporary. What is the smallest correct change for a single CommonJS script that needs one ESM-only package, and does dynamic import inside a synchronous function actually help?

title: Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite on a path type
toFixed(2) rounds 1.005 down to 1.00 and my invoice totals are off by a cent
content:
Accounting flagged a report where one line is a cent short.

```javascript
(1.005).toFixed(2);        // '1.00'
(1.015).toFixed(2);        // '1.02'
(0.1 + 0.2).toFixed(2);    // '0.30'
Math.round(1.005 * 100) / 100; // 1
```

I expected `1.01` from the first one, and the inconsistency with 1.015 is what makes it hard to explain to anyone. I know the general answer is binary floating point, but I need to decide what to actually do. The amounts come from an API as numbers with two decimals. Is the correct fix to move everything to integer cents at the boundary, or is there a rounding helper in Intl that gives the half-up behaviour the finance team expects?

Custom checkbox with appearance: none is invisible when focused by keyboard
content: Our design system replaces the native checkbox look with `appearance: none` plus a border and a background image for the tick. It looks right and it is still a real `<input type="checkbox">`, so screen readers announce it correctly. The problem came out of an audit: tabbing through the form, there is no visible indication of which checkbox is focused, because the reset also removed the default focus ring and our stylesheet has a global `*:focus { outline: none }` that predates me. Adding `outline` back on `:focus` gives a ring on mouse clicks too, which the designer rejected. I tried a `box-shadow` on `:focus` which is visible but disappears in Windows high contrast mode, and that came up in the same audit. What is the current recommended combination here so keyboard users get a ring, mouse users do not, and forced-colors mode still shows something?

title: aria-live region is not announced when React replaces the whole node
Grid column with 1fr overflows when the cell contains a long code block
content: The layout is a two-column grid, sidebar plus content, declared as `grid-template-columns: 260px 1fr`. Everything is fine until a post contains a wide `<pre>` block: instead of the code block getting its own horizontal scrollbar, the whole content column grows to the width of the longest line and the page scrolls sideways, pushing the sidebar off screen. The `<pre>` has `overflow-x: auto` on it, which I expected to be enough, and it does work if I give the column a fixed pixel width instead of `1fr`. So the grid item is somehow sizing itself to its content rather than to the track. I have seen `minmax(0, 1fr)` recommended for this and it does fix it, but I do not understand what the implicit minimum is or why `1fr` alone is not the same thing.

title: Safari returns Invalid Date for new Date('2026-01-05 10:00') but Chrome parses it
100vh hero section is taller than the viewport on iOS Safari
content: The landing hero is `height: 100vh` with a button pinned to the bottom edge. On desktop and on Android Chrome it fits exactly. On iOS Safari the button is under the browser's bottom toolbar when the page first loads, and it only becomes visible after you scroll and the toolbar collapses, which is precisely when the section is no longer the thing you are looking at. I measured `window.innerHeight` on the device and it is smaller than the value the section is getting, so `100vh` is clearly resolving against the larger, toolbar-free viewport. The usual JS workaround of writing `innerHeight` into a custom property works but reflows on every scroll and feels dated. iOS 18. Is there a viewport unit that tracks the visible area now, and what is a sane fallback for browsers that do not have it?

title: Third-party chat widget loads twice and shows two launchers in Next.js
content: We embed a support chat widget by dropping its script tag into the root layout. In production most users see one launcher bubble, but anyone who navigates client-side between two pages ends up with two, and on a hard refresh of certain routes there are briefly two before one disappears. The vendor's snippet is a plain `<script>` that appends a div to `document.body` and has no idempotency check of its own, so I assume it is running more than once. Next.js 16, App Router, the tag sits directly in the layout's JSX. I tried moving it into a client component with a `useEffect` that appends the script node, which fixed the duplicate on navigation but reintroduced it under StrictMode in dev. I would like to know what the framework offers for exactly-once third-party scripts and whether the layout is even the right place for it.
